title: Native Interoperability
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of native interoperability using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates native interoperability.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Native Interoperability** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks. Use the subtopics—C Interoperability, Objective-C and Swift Interoperability, Framework Export and Integration—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

content_blocks.text: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with c interoperability. Then compare it with objective-c and swift interoperability. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: C Interoperability
items.text: C Interoperability means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Objective-C and Swift Interoperability
items.text: Objective-C and Swift Interoperability means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Framework Export and Integration
items.text: Framework Export and Integration is one part of native interoperability. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, or Kotlin/Native project configured for the selected target. Verify platform support and maturity before production use.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Native Interoperability removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
